These conventions are now explicit; the nonempty-threat supremum, closed balls, and measurable-majorant definition are unchanged. This is a nonfatal specification omission, not a counterexample to the outer-risk definition.

The displayed finite conditional law already proves conditional independence. The reference note incorrectly omitted the conditioning law: coordinate sigma-algebras are independent under each law given Y=y (and observations under each fixed Theta=theta), not necessarily under the unconditional mixture. Repaired only that note; the Definition is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Step 2.1 attributes exp(log r)=r to F5 although that fact lists only logarithm laws and its integral formula. The already declared dependency def-natural-logarithm explicitly gives the inverse identity, so this is a nonfatal local citation omission. Added the identity and its exact existing supplier to F5. Both branches, constants, posterior independence, zero-weight/no-sample cases and strict radius<1 threshold invariance remain sound; Statement is unchanged.

F1 bounds the normalized-or-fallback direction and does not exclude W=0, so the original inference W!=0 and consequent replacement of f_W by f_U had an unsupported logical step. Repaired Proof 1.1: conditional on all labels, the independent scalar normals Y_i X_i1 have mean theta_1 and variance sigma^2; their average is N(theta_1,sigma^2/n), hence atomless and P(W=0)<=P(W_1=0)=0. Removing this null event preserves the alignment probability and the positive normalization. Statement, constants, closed radius and tie convention are unchanged.
